Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Allergy & Immunology
Visit Type: outpatient

- Atopic dermatitis
- Pulmonary pneumatoceles (status post recurrent Staphylococcal pneumonia)

- Incision and drainage of cutaneous abscesses (multiple episodes)

NKDA

- Mother: Autosomal Dominant Hyper-IgE Syndrome (eczema, recurrent skin infections)
- Father: Healthy
- Maternal grandfather: History of severe eczema and 'cold' abscesses

Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Pre-kindergarten student.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2022-01-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Johnson, MD
Department: Pediatrics
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
High fever for three days with cough, runny nose, and frequent eye rubbing

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient with autosomal dominant Hyper-IgE syndrome diagnosed in 2020 returns for evaluation. The parents report that he has been coughing, has a runny nose, and has been rubbing his eyes frequently. The child has not been vaccinated due to parental concerns.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Job syndrome (Autosomal Dominant Hyper-IgE Syndrome) (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Atopic dermatitis
- Pulmonary pneumatoceles (status post recurrent Staphylococcal pneumonia)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Incision and drainage of cutaneous abscesses (multiple episodes)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Topical triamcinolone acetonide 0.1% ointment Apply thin layer to affected skin BID PRN for eczema flare
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole suspension 5 mL (40 mg/200 mg) PO BID for Staphylococcus aureus prophylaxis

ALLERGIES:
He has no known drug allergies.

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Mother: Autosomal Dominant Hyper-IgE Syndrome (eczema, recurrent skin infections)
- Father: Healthy
- Maternal grandfather: History of severe eczema and 'cold' abscesses

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Pre-kindergarten student.

VITAL SIGNS:
His vital signs are as follows:

- Temperature: 39.5°C (103.1°F)
- Pulse: 110/min
- Respirations: 24/min
- Blood pressure: 100/60 mmHg

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, the boy appears irritable and has red, watery eyes without purulent discharge. Inspection of the oral cavity reveals small white lesions on the buccal mucosa. A maculopapular rash is noted on his face and seems to be spreading to his trunk.

attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2024-01-15
Provider: Dr. Elena Rodriguez, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Worsening rash and high fever reaching 40°C (104°F) over the past three days

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient is an 8-year-old male with autosomal dominant hyper-IgE syndrome (Job syndrome) and a history of wild-type measles infection in 2022 who presents with worsening rash and high fever over the past three days. The fever initially was 38.9°C (102°F) but has since increased to 40°C (104°F). The rash began as small red spots with blue-white centers on the inside of his mouth, and the following day it spread to his face and then to his trunk and extremities. The parents also report that the child has had decreased appetite and has been less active than usual.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Job syndrome (Autosomal Dominant Hyper-IgE Syndrome) (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Measles (wild-type) (diagnosed 2022-01-15)
- Atopic dermatitis
- Pulmonary pneumatoceles (status post recurrent Staphylococcal pneumonia)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Incision and drainage of cutaneous abscesses (multiple episodes)

MEDICATIONS:
He takes topical steroids.

Home Medications:
- Topical triamcinolone acetonide 0.1% ointment Apply thin layer to affected skin BID PRN for eczema flare
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole suspension 5 mL (40 mg/200 mg) PO BID for Staphylococcus aureus prophylaxis

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Mother: Autosomal Dominant Hyper-IgE Syndrome (eczema, recurrent skin infections)
- Father: Healthy
- Maternal grandfather: History of severe eczema and 'cold' abscesses

SOCIAL HISTORY:
He has not received any vaccinations due to his parents' preferences

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
The child appears lethargic and has a generalized maculopapular rash. His conjunctivae are injected, and there is coryza and a dry cough.

LABORATORY DATA:
- Hemoglobin: 11.2 g/dL
- Leukocyte count: 4500/mm³ with lymphopenia
- Platelets: 150,000/mm³
- Serum sodium: 133 mEq/L
- C-reactive protein: 20 mg/L
